segments: The Chronography of Bar Hebraeus. [Page 220]
And the teacher replied:
"Yes."
And that boy retorted to him:
"So then, if someone asks me what a human being is,
is it right that I tell him, 'an animal'?" And the teacher replied:
"Yes."
And that boy disputed against him and said:
"I do not agree to this,
nor am I so utterly devoid of understanding
that if someone asks me about something that is a rational animal,
I should return to him only 'animal',
which is half of an answer!"
And from then on he left the teacher,
and on his own he would read all the disciplines and comprehend them.
And when he was sixteen years old,
he had excelled so greatly in medicine
that many aged physicians would come to him and study under him.
And he also began to visit the sick,
and he became proficient also in clinical practice.
And when he was eighteen years old,
he wrote this great and renowned book of the Canon.
And afterwards he wrote the great book of Healing (Kitab al-Shifa) in the four disciplines of philosophy,
completing the physics and metaphysics of this book within twenty days.
Now his books which are found and read are
ninety-two books,
and the majority of them he composed in prison.
And one marvelous book among his books, which is called 'Pointers and Reminders' (al-Isharat wa-l-Tanbihat),
I, the feeble one, have translated from Arabic into Syriac.
For he was captured in the defeat that befell the ruler whom he served,
by another ruler, his enemy,
and he was imprisoned in one of the fortresses.
And as he was entering, he said:
"In my entry here there is absolutely no doubt;
but upon my exit, in truth, all kinds of hardship {or: uncertainty? / Arabic: fartaka?} attend."
Now he remained there forty days,
until that ruler of his came,
took the fortress by battle,
and brought him out.
And apart from this occasion,
he was also imprisoned at other times.
And despite all this excellence which that preeminent master possessed,
the carnal passion for sexual intercourse used to overpower him.
And this condition weakened his strength,
and his constitution was shaken,
and at the end of his days he developed the pain of colic.
And in a single day,
he administered an enema to himself eight times.
And when he ordered that two dānaqs of celery seed be put into the enema,
one of his servants put in five dirhams;
